author: Daniel Greene
description:
Agatha Christie's Five Little Pigs is one of her most emotional and unusual mysteries — no active crime scene, no fresh body, just five suspects and memories that may or may not be true. Hercule Poirot must solve a murder that happened 16 years ago using nothing but testimony. I read it blind and tried to solve it before the ending. And for the first time ever — I actually did it.
Is Five Little Pigs Christie at her best? I think it might be.
